"You look for the assumption that makes a problem slow, or makes extra compute buy only more of the same. Ask which part
of the work waits on another part, and whether it must. Ask which quantity is measured, and whether a different but
related quantity would be cheaper to compute, easier to split, or more informative. Ask whether the unit of work is the
right one, or whether the work could be cut, merged or reordered. Ask whether the objective is the right one: the single
best answer, a ranking, a distribution, a rare tail, or a yes or no. Ask what is held fixed that need not be. Prefer
changes that alter what more compute buys over changes that only run the same work more times.

Here is a research problem as it was first written down, with the question it belongs to.
Root question: What's actually stopping general purpose robot hands from reliably doing stuff like folding laundry or loading a dishwasher? Is it the lack of real-world manipulation data, the hardware (sensors, actuators, tactile feedback), or the sim-to-real gap? Is that a major blocker at some level, and could it be fixed by running millions of simulated robots in parallel on a shit ton of GPUs?
Problem:
Inference-time steering of VLA internals (SAEs, FFN vectors, conceptors, linear observers)
Steering a VLA's internal features can bring out behaviour the model already has, without retraining. On real DROID hardware, SAE steering of pi0.5 raised target-object grasps by +9 to +21 out of 25 trials, and ablating the top-4 general features cut success from 39/40 to 0/40. COAST conceptors raised pi0.5 on LIBERO-10 from 0.43 to 0.80, with about +40% on three real tasks. Grant et al. found motor programs bound to absolute coordinates (50/50 grasps at the recorded spot on a UR10e). All tests are rigid tabletop tasks; none is cloth or a dish rack. Goodfire markets steering for robotics but publishes no numbers.
What more compute would buy: The quantity is closed-loop rollouts and SAEs swept; the largest is 420,000+ rollouts and 520+ SAEs across six VLAs (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19233), and above that it is unknown whether any feature controls contact-rich or deformable behaviour, because every sweep so far ran rigid pick-and-place or drawer tasks.
What runs step after step: Each feature waits on an SAE fit (about 6,700 Adam steps, derived from https://arxiv.org/html/2603.19183; 'a few GPU-hours per SAE on one A100') and then on closed-loop rollouts of up to 300 steps, each waiting on a ~150 ms VLA forward pass and the next observation; the answer needed 150 rollouts × 135 features (20,250 episodes), and one unbatched rollout leaves the GPU idle while the simulator steps. Steps within a rollout must run in order, but rollouts are independent: batching hundreds of steered environments in a GPU-parallel simulator, with a separate hook per environment and simulation pipelined against inference, would run them together; this pays only if steering effects in simulation match the real robot (false for cloth). The nearest attempt is RLinf-VLA, 1.61-1.88x with 256 ManiSkill environments, for RL rather than interpretability (https://arxiv.org/html/2510.06710v2).

Find where this problem stops more compute from helping, or where more compute only buys more of the same. Then look for reframings: changes to what is measured, the unit of work, the objective or the order of steps that would let more compute change the answer. Give up to three. End each with one question someone could investigate: specific, answerable by a measurement, and naming what is measured. For each, give the cheapest measurement that would answer it or show it is not worth pursuing, with a rough cost. Decide from the text above and what you know; do not use tools.

Return only one JSON value, with no other text, that matches this JSON Schema:
{\"type\":\"object\",\"required\":[\"reframes\"],\"properties\":{\"reframes\":{\"type\":\"array\",\"items\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"required\":[\"bottleneck\",\"assumption\",\"reframe\",\"question\",\"measure\",\"compute_after\",\"exact\",\"expected\",\"fails_if\",\"closest_prior\"],\"properties\":{\"bottleneck\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"assumption\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"reframe\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"question\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"measure\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"compute_after\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"exact\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"expected\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"fails_if\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"closest_prior\":{\"type\":\"string\"}}}}}}"

We need answer only JSON matching schema. Need think through problem deeply. We have user prompt includes research problem. We need produce up to three reframes with fields: bottleneck, assumption, reframe, question, measure, compute_after, exact, expected, fails_if, closest_prior. No tools. Need decide from text and knowledge. Need produce exact JSON no markdown.

Let's parse problem. Root question: robot hands laundry/dishwasher blockers: data, hardware, sim-to-real; can millions simulated robots fix? Specific problem: inference-time steering of VLA internals (SAEs, FFN vectors, conceptors, linear observers). Steering can elicit behavior without retraining. Evidence: DROID pi0.5 SAE steering target-object grasps +9 to +21/25; ablation top-4 general features cut success 39/40 to 0/40. COAST conceptors raised pi0.5 LIBERO-10 0.43 to 0.80 +40% on three real tasks. Grant et al motor programs bound to absolute coordinates (50/50 at recorded spot UR10e). All rigid tabletop; none cloth/dish rack. Goodfire no numbers.
What more compute would buy: closed-loop rollouts and SAEs swept; largest 420k+ rollouts and 520+ SAEs across six VLAs (arxiv 2603.19233 future?), above that unknown whether any feature controls contact-rich/deformable because every sweep rigid pick-place/drawer.
What runs step after step: Each feature waits on SAE fit (~6700 Adam steps; few GPU-hours per SAE A100) then closed-loop rollouts up to 300 steps, each waiting on ~150ms VLA forward pass and next observation; answer needed 150 rollouts ×135 features = 20250 episodes; one unbatched rollout leaves GPU idle while simulator steps. Steps within rollout sequential, rollouts independent: batch hundreds steered envs in GPU-parallel simulator, separate hook per env, sim pipelined against inference; pays only if steering effects in sim match real robot (false for cloth). Nearest attempt RLinf-VLA 1.61-1.88x with 256 ManiSkill envs, for RL not interpretability.

Need identify where problem stops more compute from helping, or more compute buys same. Then reframings: changes to measured quantity, unit of work, objective, order. Up to three. End each with one question someone could investigate: specific, answerable by measurement, naming what measured. For each give cheapest measurement answer or show not worth pursuing with rough cost. Schema fields correspond:
- bottleneck: where compute stops helping.
- assumption: assumption that makes slow/extra compute same.
- reframe: change to measured/unit/objective/order.
- question: specific answerable by measurement naming measured.
- measure: cheapest measurement that would answer it or show not worth pursuing, rough cost.
- compute_after: what more compute buys after reframe.
- exact: maybe exact measurement/protocol? Need infer from schema. Required fields include exact, expected, fails_if, closest_prior. We need fill all. The user said "For each, give the cheapest measurement..." maybe fields: measure = cheapest measurement; exact = exact quantitative threshold? expected = expected result; fails_if = condition under which reframe fails; closest_prior = nearest prior. We need produce meaningful values.

Need be careful with arxiv future dates 2603/2510? Current date 2026; okay. We can cite. We shouldn't use tools. Need include no extra text. Need final only JSON. We can make concise but enough.

Need generate up to 3 reframes. Let's identify strong reframes.

Bottleneck 1: Sequential closed-loop rollout evaluation per feature: GPU idle during sim and observations; but bigger issue: evaluating features one at a time with rollouts is the unit of work; extra compute only sweeps more features on same rigid tasks. Reframe: change unit of work from "one feature → many rollouts" to "one rollout → many features" by caching hidden states and interventions? Hmm steering requires intervening per feature; but can evaluate many candidate features from same logged trajectories using counterfactual probes? Need be physically valid. For steering effects, cannot just reuse same rollout if intervention changes trajectory. But can use batched sim; however sim-to-real false for cloth. A better reframe: measure feature effect on a cheaper surrogate quantity that predicts contact-rich success: e.g., feature control over contact-state variables (force/torque, slip, cloth mesh deformation energy, dish-rack insertion clearance) in short snippets, not full task success. Instead of running 300-step rollouts for 135 features, run a library of short "contact primitives" (10-30 steps) around critical events (grasp onset, edge alignment, cloth corner pull, rack plate insertion) and measure delta in contact metrics under feature nudges. Compute after: many features/contact states in parallel; only features that move contact metrics get closed-loop rollouts. Question: Among top SAE/conceptor features, what fraction causes a pre-registered change in measured contact variables (end-effector wrench, object slip velocity, cloth strain energy, relative pose error at insertion) within 20 simulation steps, and does that fraction predict 300-step success lift on held-out contact-rich tasks? Cheapest measurement: build 3 GPU-sim contact snippets with force/torque and deformable state logging (e.g., Isaac Gym/MuJoCo FLEX? soft body) plus 20 features, run 50 short snippets each = maybe 1000×20-step = 20k steps; one A100 day. Compare with known real rigid steering features. Fails if contact metrics not predictive. Closest prior: RLinf-VLA batching; ManiSkill; DROID/SAE steering.

But field asks question someone could investigate specific, answerable by measurement, naming what measured. We can put in question. measure field cheapest measurement. compute_after maybe "a 135-feature sweep becomes a contact-metric screen followed by rollouts for survivors; parallel short snippets scale with GPU envs, and more compute buys coverage of contact states rather than repeated rigid successes." exact: maybe exact thresholds: ">10% change in contact metric with |Δ| exceeding 2× noise and predicts success with AUC>0.8". expected: "most features do nothing; small set moves insertion clearance/slip; AUC ~0.75-0.9 for rigid; unknown for cloth." fails_if: "short-horizon contact deltas have AUC <0.6 or confidence intervals include chance for held-out 300-step success." closest_prior: "SAE sweep 420k rollouts/520 SAEs; RLinf-VLA 256 ManiSkill envs; LIBERO/COAST."

Need maybe not overly numerical invented? We can include rough. Since current date weird and arxiv numbers future, okay.

Bottleneck 2: Objective is single-best task success / binary success; extra rollouts only estimate same Bernoulli for rigid tasks. Reframe objective to a distributional/rare-tail quantity: measure whether steering shifts the tail of failure modes relevant to laundry/dishwashing (recovery after slip, regrasp, collision force, cloth entanglement) rather than average success. For deformable/dish rack, rare tail and recovery matter. Unit of work: paired perturbation trials at decision points; measure causal effect of features on failure probability under injected disturbances (slip, object offset, cloth wrinkle, rack position noise) and on recovery time. More compute buys tail resolution: importance sampling / subset simulation around failures, many parallel perturbations. Question: Does any steering feature reduce the conditional probability of high-force/slip failure given a standard perturbation (e.g., 1 cm object displacement, 0.5 N friction drop, cloth corner folded) by at least 5 percentage points without increasing collision-force tail, measured as P(fail|perturb, steering on/off) and recovery steps? Cheapest measurement: pick 3 candidate features from rigid screens, 2 perturbations per task (object offset and friction/slip), 100 paired short episodes in sim and 20 paired real trials on one dish-rack insertion or towel-corner grasp = maybe 240 sim episodes (short) + 120 real trials; cost one A100 day + 2-3 robot-days. Exact: lower CI on ΔP_fail < -0.05 and no >+10 N in 95th percentile contact force; recovery steps reduced ≥25%. Expected: steering features found in rigid grasp mostly move target selection not contact tail; a few general features affect recovery; on deformable no effect. Fails_if: perturbation response is smaller than trial noise (CI crosses zero after 20 real paired trials) or high-force tail worsens. Closest_prior: COAST, SAE steering, Grant absolute coords, Goodfire; robustness/perturbation evals in manipulation.

But the instruction says "Ask whether the objective is the right one: the single best answer, a ranking, a distribution, a rare tail, or a yes or no." So reframe objective to rare tail/yes/no. Good.

Bottleneck 3: Assumption: features must be found by fitting SAEs separately per model/layer then evaluating; SAE fit serial before measurement. Also quantity measured maybe "does a feature exist" not "is there a linear direction cheap to estimate". Reframe: skip unsupervised SAE for screening; use supervised linear probes / conceptors / difference-in-means targeted at contact-rich outcome to find candidate directions, and order steps: cheap real/sim contact data collection first, fit probes for all layers in parallel, then closed-loop validation. More compute buys breadth across models/tasks, not more SAEs. But the problem already includes linear observers/conceptors. Need a sharper reframe: Change what is measured from internal-feature identity (SAE index) to an intervention's transferable causal effect across coordinate frames and tasks. Since Grant et al found motor programs bound to absolute coordinates, a key blocker for laundry/dish rack is pose generalization: features may encode absolute recorded spots, not relative object/hand contact geometry. More compute sweeping SAEs on fixed tabletop only buys same absolute-coordinate successes. Reframe unit/objective: evaluate steering in a relative frame: randomize object pose and camera/base each trial; measure the fraction of effect retained under SE(3) transforms (pose-generalization half-life) and whether steering in a learned object-relative coordinate frame restores it. Question: When target object pose is randomized over the workspace, what is the measured pose-generalization curve of each steering effect (success vs radial/angular displacement from training pose), and does transforming the steering vector into an object-relative frame (from detected pose) keep success within 10% of the recorded-pose effect at 20 cm/45°? Cheapest measurement: choose 1 known steering feature with +9/+21 DROID effect and 1 ablation-critical feature; run 25 recorded-pose trials + 5×5 grid at 5/10/20 cm and 15/30/45° with and without object-relative transform on one real task and mirrored sim; ~150-250 real trials, 3-5 robot days, no new SAE (or few GPU hours if probe). Compute_after: if object-relative transform restores effect, parallel pose-randomized sweeps can measure generalization across many features/tasks; more compute buys map of feature frame-dependence; if not, stop sweeping steering as path to laundry. Exact: measure retention R = (success_steered - success_base) at displacement / same at recorded pose; require R≥0.8 at 20cm/45° after relative transform; without transform expect R decays to ~0 by 10-20 cm if absolute-coordinate binding. Expected: many VLA motor features are absolute-pose bound; object-relative steering helps if model encodes pose in a transformable way; likely partial for pi0.5 because DROID has varying poses but motor programs maybe absolute (Grant UR10e). Fails_if: relative transform cannot recover R above 0.5 at 10 cm, or detected pose noise (≥1 cm/2°) accounts for drop—then steering is not the blocker; hardware/state estimation is. Closest_prior: Grant et al absolute coordinates 50/50 UR10e; SAE steering DROID; COAST conceptors.

This one is strong, directly root question hardware/sim-to-real. It changes measured quantity (effect retention under SE(3)) and order (pose randomization before large sweeps). Good.

Need ensure each reframe ends with one question. In our JSON, question field contains one question. It says end each with one question someone could investigate. Maybe each reframe object's narrative should end with question? Since fields fixed, we can make question field the question; maybe also reframe field end with question? But schema doesn't enforce. We can make "question" specific. "End each" maybe means each reframe should end with one question; in JSON order maybe question field after reframe? Schema order properties listed bottleneck, assumption, reframe, question, measure, compute_after, exact, expected, fails_if, closest_prior. But JSON object order irrelevant. Yet to satisfy, make the "question" field directly after reframe and have it be the question. Fine.

Need include exact field. We need interpret "exact" maybe exact wording of question? Let's infer. The schema includes "exact" and "expected" and "fails_if". Maybe "exact" means the exact measurement/estimand (statistics), "expected" expected outcome, "fails_if" invalidation. We can set exact to the precise estimand/threshold. Good.

Need maybe include "compute_after" as what more compute buys after reframe. Good.

Need answer only JSON value. Need ensure valid JSON with escaping. No markdown. No trailing commas. Need maybe quote URLs? Fine. Need no unescaped newline? JSON can include pretty printed with newlines. That's okay; one JSON value. We can output pretty JSON. It says no other text. Good.

Need craft final with array length 3. Need strings concise but complete. Use rough costs. Need mention current arxiv links? In closest_prior maybe include names. Avoid fake arxiv? The prompt gives arxiv future. We can cite them as "the 420k-rollout/520-SAE sweep (arXiv:2603.19233)". Fine.

Need be precise about "above that it is unknown whether any feature controls contact-rich or deformable behavior". Reframe #1: Instead of asking "is there a feature" via full rollouts, measure causal control over contact variables in short windows. But if sim false for cloth, using sim for cloth may fail. We can use real cheap proxy? For cloth, maybe use a benchtop deformable proxy with sensors (marked cloth, force-torque) and short primitive. The cheapest measurement to answer or show not worth pursuing: use one real deformable/contact primitive not full laundry: pulling a towel corner taut over a peg or inserting a plate into a rack, with a wrist FT camera and AprilTags; run paired short interventions for candidate features. Cost: candidate features from existing SAEs (no fit) + 100 paired trials = 1-2 robot days; if need new SAE one A100 few GPU-hours. But we need answer question: does feature control contact-rich/deformable? The cheapest measurement: pick top features from rigid sweeps and general/ablation features; test on a 10-step "contact microtask" with measurable contact variables. More compute after: parallel screen of thousands features against contact variables, then full rollouts only for candidates. Good.

Maybe separate reframe #1 and #3 overlap. #1 measured quantity: contact variables not success. #3 pose generalization/relative frame. #2 objective rare tail/perturbation. Good.

Let's formulate fields.

Reframe 1:
- bottleneck: "Evaluation is serialized per feature: fit SAE → run up to 300-step closed-loop rollouts; one unbatched rollout idles the GPU, and after 150×135 episodes more of the same only estimates rigid-task success more precisely."
- assumption: "The right measured quantity is whole-episode success for one steered feature at a time, and a feature must be validated by a full rollout before anything is known about contact control."
- reframe: "Change the unit of work to a short paired contact-window intervention: for each candidate direction, steer on/off for 10-30 steps around a canonical event (grasp onset, plate-at-rack mouth, towel-corner pull) and measure Δ in contact state, not task success. Use these windows as a screen; only directions that move contact variables earn long rollouts."
- question: "For the top 50 existing SAE/conceptor directions and 50 random matched controls, what fraction produces |Δ| > 2 noise SD in at least one measured contact variable (wrist F/T, object slip speed, insertion clearance, cloth strain energy from marker motion) within 20 steps, and what AUC does that contact Δ have for held-out 300-step success?"
- measure: "Use already-fit features; add one real instrumented microtask (plate into rack + towel corner over peg) and one matching GPU sim. Run 100 paired on/off windows ×100 directions in sim (20-step windows; ~40k steps, <1 A100-day) and 20 paired real windows for the 20 most promising directions (400 short trials, ~1-2 robot-days). Rough cost: <$1k GPU plus 2 robot-days; no new SAE sweep."
- compute_after: "Thousands of directions can be screened in parallel short windows; extra compute buys coverage of directions, layers, objects and contact states, then concentrates closed-loop rollouts on the few causal candidates and the contact regimes where they act."
- exact: "Estimand: paired on/off change in contact variables during steps 5-25; positive if a direction has same-sign effect in ≥60% of windows, bootstrap CI excluding 2 SD noise, and contact-Δ score predicts held-out success with AUC ≥0.8 (screen useful) or ≤0.6 (not worth pursuing)."
- expected: "Most directions are inert; a small set changes slip/clearance for rigid insertion; deformable cloth effect is likely weak or entangled with visual/pose features. Screen should cut full rollouts by ~10-50× if AUC is high."
- fails_if: "Contact-window Δ has AUC <0.6 for held-out success, real/sim sign disagreement for the same rigid microtask, or the effect is present only when the camera/pose is held fixed."
- closest_prior: "Largest SAE sweep: 420k+ rollouts and 520+ SAEs across six VLAs (arXiv:2603.19233); SAE fitting cost from arXiv:2603.19183; parallel VLA rollouts: RLinf-VLA with 256 ManiSkill envs (arXiv:2510.06710v2)."

Need maybe exact AUC threshold okay.

Reframe 2:
- bottleneck: "The objective is average/binary success on unperturbed rigid tasks; once a feature is shown to help pick-and-place, additional episodes buy the same point estimate and do not resolve laundry/dishwasher failures, which live in tails: slip, high force, entanglement, recovery."
- assumption: "A feature that raises mean success is useful for reliable household manipulation; perturbations need not be injected because they are rare or will be handled by the same policy."
- reframe: "Change the objective to a paired rare-tail/robustness claim: measure conditional failure and recovery under standard disturbances (object offset, friction drop, cloth wrinkle, rack mis-seat). Use importance sampling/subset simulation in parallel to resolve the tail, and accept a direction only if it lowers failure probability without raising the high-force tail."
- question: "Under a fixed perturbation set (1 cm/5° object offset, 30% friction drop, one cloth corner folded, 5 mm rack misalignment), does any candidate direction reduce measured P(failure | perturbation) by ≥5 percentage points and reduce recovery steps by ≥25%, while not increasing the 95th-percentile contact force by >10 N?"
- measure: "Cheapest gate: 2 candidate directions ×2 perturbations ×100 paired short sim episodes (=400 episodes; <1 A100-day with batched envs) and 20 paired real trials per direction-perturbation on plate insertion and towel-corner pull (=160 real short trials, ~2 robot-days) with FT sensor and marker/AprilTag logging. Rough cost: <$1k GPU + 2-3 robot-days."
- compute_after: "More compute buys tail resolution via parallel perturbed episodes and rare-event splitting across objects, disturbance magnitudes and VLA checkpoints; it changes the answer from 'helps on average' to 'changes the failure distribution'."
- exact: "Report ΔP_fail = P_fail(on)-P_fail(off) per perturbation with paired bootstrap CI; pass only if upper CI < -0.05, median recovery steps ratio ≤0.75, and ΔF95 ≤ +10 N. Fail-fast if after 20 real paired trials the CI half-width exceeds 0.10."
- expected: "Rigid target-selection features likely move mean grasp choice but not slip/high-force tails; general features ablated in the 39/40→0/40 test may affect recovery, but for cloth the effect may vanish outside the recorded pose."
- fails_if: "No direction clears ΔP_fail ≤ -0.05 without force-tail increase, or perturbation failures are dominated by perception/state-estimation error rather than steerable motor/contact features."
- closest_prior: "COAST conceptors on LIBERO-10 and three real tasks; pi0.5 SAE steering/ablation on DROID; Goodfire steering claims without numbers; robustness evaluations are scarcer than success sweeps."

Reframe 3:
- bottleneck: "The sweep holds task coordinate frame and evaluation distribution nearly fixed; Grant-style absolute-coordinate motor programs mean more rollouts at the recorded spot can keep buying 50/50 successes while saying nothing about laundry/dish racks in new poses."
- assumption: "An internal steering vector represents a portable skill; moving the object/base/camera should preserve the intervention, so pose randomization is an unnecessary cost."
- reframe: "Measure steering as a function of SE(3) displacement and re-express the intervention in an object-relative frame before scaling. Order steps as: estimate pose → transform steering vector/hook → randomized-pose microtrial → only then large sweep."
- question: "For a known effective pi0.5/DROID direction, what is the measured retention curve R(d,θ)=(success_on-success_off at displacement)/(success_on-success_off at recorded pose) over d∈{0,5,10,20} cm and θ∈{0,15,30,45}°, and does object-relative transformation keep R(20 cm,45°) ≥0.8 while the untransformed vector falls below 0.5?"
- measure: "No new SAE: reuse one known positive direction and one ablation-critical direction. On one real insertion/grasp task run 25 baseline paired trials at recorded pose plus a 4×4 pose grid, 10 paired trials per cell, with and without relative transform: 25 + 16 cells×10×2 = 345 short trials; ~3-5 robot-days with AprilTag pose and FT logging; mirror in sim for <1 A100-day to select grid. Rough cost: primarily robot time, <$1k GPU."
- compute_after: "If relative transformation restores R, parallel pose-randomized sweeps can rank features by generalization half-life across tasks and models; more compute buys a map of which internal directions are portable and which are absolute-coordinate memories."
- exact: "Primary estimand R(d,θ) with paired CI; decision: portable only if R≥0.8 at (20 cm,45°) after transform and untransformed R≤0.5 at same point. Also report pose-estimation error and success drop explained by it (e.g., R after adding measured pose noise to the transform)."
- expected: "Untransformed steering decays quickly with displacement if it encodes absolute motor programs; object-relative transformation helps only when the VLA has a usable pose representation, so expected outcome is partial recovery for insertion and poor recovery for cloth if pose/cloth state is uncertain."
- fails_if: "Object-relative transform does not raise R above ~0.5 at 10 cm/15°, or the residual failure is fully explained by ≥1 cm/2° pose-estimation error; then more steering compute is not the blocker and hardware/state estimation should be fixed first."
- closest_prior: "Grant et al. absolute-coordinate motor programs (50/50 at recorded UR10e spot); pi0.5 SAE steering on DROID (+9 to +21/25) and top-4 ablation 39/40→0/40; COAST pi0.5 gains on LIBERO/real tasks."
